correctness.rationale: The stationary alternating-renewal age law gives Pr(A>s|orientation)=H(s)/m. The positive-run deficit is Z=Z0 exp(-kappa A) and, after a negative run of length U, Z0>=1-exp(-kappa U). This yields matching upper/lower support-edge bounds with exponentially negligible short-U exceptions, using Pr(T<=u)=O(u^beta). Karamata gives H(s)~s Pr(T>s)/(alpha-1), proving the exact equivalent. The half-t density has survival 1-t/sqrt(t^2+tau^2), H(t)=sqrt(t^2+tau^2)-t and m=tau. A window shrinking as O(log s) yields the explicit relative O(log s/s) error. The standalone checker validates algebraic identities, finite bounds and Monte Carlo diagnostics, not the infinite asymptotic.
